content.value: What are the advantages successive approximation counter have over counter type ADC? (14) Illustrate the process of converting 12 V analog input into digital output in a 4-bit successive approximation ADC with $\mathtt { V } _ { \mathtt { r e f } } = 1 6 \mathtt { V }$ . Given output of R-2R ADC,

$\begin{array} { r } { \hat { \mathrm { V } } _ { \mathrm { o u t } } = \mathrm { b } _ { 3 } \frac { \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { r e f } } } { 2 } + \mathrm { b } _ { 2 } \frac { \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { r e f } } } { 4 } + \mathrm { b } _ { 3 } \frac { \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { r e f } } } { 8 } + \mathrm { b } _ { 0 } \frac { \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { r e f } } } { 1 6 } } \end{array}$ where ${ \sf b } _ { 3 }$ corresponds to bit $3 , \mathsf { b } _ { 2 }$ to bit 2 etc.
